node_definition.done_when:
Build the read as one vectorised fixed-shape kernel with no data-dependent loops, then put it inside the fused moment-Newton program and re-measure the warm slice. Lead ruling 2026-10-15, after both prototypes pointed at the read as the remaining bottleneck.

Where it stands (all on main):
- docs/research/read-robustness.html (merged at cfee999d7): the full-row read with a mobile gather and a root census reads 36/41 limited and 32/41 diverted states valid with the correct axis; the rest have no converged analytic oracle or a root outside the wall. It costs 12 to 15 ms. Booked current still jumps 7.8e-6 of target at the limited-to-diverted switch, a class-dependent support discontinuity.
- docs/research/fused-moment-newton.html (merged at 896f97d13): the fused program still calls topology.read_at_stationary_points (strip fori_loops and min-label while_loops) and repeats the map for each of four JVPs. One correction therefore launches about 14,000 kernels and costs 26 to 36 ms against 0.90 ms. No width-128 member converges, and compiles take 108 to 120 s.
- docs/research/sub-millisecond-forward-design.html: measured fast owners for each stage.
  - Saddle-frame-gated wall-domain graph: 179/179 cells, 0.361 ms.
  - Four-arc closed-form Bell cut: about 0.3 ms.
  - 18-point Gauss interior: 0.244 ms.
  - Dense values map: 0.144 ms.
  - fixed_points roots: 0.317 ms.
- The lead rules the limited-to-diverted transition continuous: both boundary candidates are computed every step, and no discrete verdict feeds the iteration.

Done when docs/research/fast-fixed-shape-read.html (reckon-type research, plan-informs converged-forward-solve) reports these measurements on the H200 at 282 diverted and 289 limited cells:
(1) A read kernel with only static shapes and no while_loop or fori_loop over cells, strips or labels:
- Boundary candidates: the X-point and limiter-contact boundary fluxes are computed every step from the roots and the wall-node flux, and the binding one is selected without a branch.
- Membership: decided per cell from its Bell polynomial at nodes and edges, vectorised over cells.
- Connectivity: from the saddle-frame-gated graph, or dense boolean reachability at this size, instead of fragment labels.
- Cut cells: booked by the four-arc closed form, including the saddle cut, vectorised.
- Bell rows: through the single owner fixed_points.maintain_rows, not a duplicate window policy; at about 300 cells it may read every row.
- Roots: the read-robustness census and continuation.
(2) Validity on the read-robustness 41-state vertical-field sweeps for both topologies: valid wherever the analytic oracle converges, with axis position and identity on every state.
(3) Continuity through the limited-to-diverted transition: boundary flux and booked current continuous to roundoff across a bisected bracket, closing the 7.8e-6 jump.
(4) Cost: wall per read and kernel launches per read, counted with the JAX profiler. Target at most 0.12 ms and tens of kernels; report what remains if missed.
(5) Integration into the fused program, measured on the H200:
- A cached factor replaces the four JVP maps per correction.
- Warm-slice wall against the 0.90 ms table, and cold solve.
- jax.vmap throughput at batch widths 1, 16 and 128 over distinct states, with the count that converges to 1e-12.
- Cold compile and executable size against 60 s and 50 MB.
(6) Map error against the analytic certificates and JVP against finite differences for the new read.
(7) Figures under docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/fast-read, following AGENTS.md plotting rules:
- one poloidal line-contour panel per terminal forward state, showing solved and analytic flux on shared levels, both null sets and the wall, with no axes;
- the 41-state sweep validity and axis map;
- wall and kernel count per stage.
Negative controls must re-run the program rather than read a frozen receipt:
- an ungated private-cell edge turns the map-error row red;
- a wrong-axis root that a convergence-only check accepts turns the axis-identity row red.

Write only scripts/prototypes/fast_read, docs/research/fast-fixed-shape-read.html, docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/fast-read and docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/fast-read.html, with plan-evidence-for converged-forward-solve. Import, but do not edit, scripts/prototypes/{read_robustness,fused_newton,sub_millisecond,lean_map} and nova/. Do not change nova/ product code, and do not touch the held moment-space Newton worktree. reckon audit-doc must report 0 errors.

Run conditions: H200 rows run as one job through RECKON_ALLOW_NESTED_LAUNCH=1 scripts/h200_test_lane/run.sh --log (an absolute path in the run directory) --wait -- (targets), or one sbatch job on --partition=betelgeuse --reservation=gpu_0003_grpA --gres=gpu:1 with rungs as rows inside the allocation (never an array), --time sized to finish, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false and TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment and in every child; submit for real and read squeue a minute later rather than trusting sbatch --test-only. On a compute node run /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python directly with PYTHONPATH set to the run worktree and never invoke uv; every login-node uv command carries --no-sync and nothing runs uv sync. configure_dtypes() before any array and jax_enable_x64 asserted True. Gates pass by delta against orientation_base_sha in per-module fresh processes, both arms running the same test files with the repository root conftest, baseline_suite and after_suite as single-line JSON whose log_path names one log file and whose command is literally runnable. Any wait is declared on the job that finishes last as wait_probe ["sacct","-n","-X","-P","-j","(job id)","-o","State"] and wait_terminal ["COMPLETED","FAILED","CANCELLED","TIMEOUT","OUT_OF_MEMORY","NODE_FAIL"] as JSON lists, and names every job it depends on in wait_condition. The certified 550, 2,000 and 5,000-cell machines and exteriors are cached under /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261009T181553786165-proto-support/ordered/rows/cache and may be read in place, never written. Run filepath relativize over any evidence fragment before committing. Commit with conventional subjects and bodies at every step and write the manifest and commit before every job wait; the manifest commits line lists every commit; status is complete, blocked or failed, which the worker sets itself. No plan labels in source names or comments. Inside every job payload, make one directory with mktemp -d /tmp/$USER-$SLURM_JOB_ID-XXXX, point TMPDIR at it, and remove it on exit with trap 'rm -rf' (keep TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment so slurmstepd can start). Never leave extracted base trees or caches in /tmp after a node ends; anything a later reader needs goes under the run directory on GPFS.

Import provenance: print nova.__file__ in every log header. On the fleet allocation (SLURM_JOB_ID set), run CPU work in place. The time budget is per working turn, not a deadline: park on H200 jobs with declared waits and continue across turns; this node is sized at about 8 worker-hours, and an unmeasured item in your own scope is remaining work, not a blocker. Never edit a script a submitted job will run; submit a per-job copy. Size every job memory from a measured row. The manifest commits line lists every commit (git rev-list), orientation_base_sha is copied from git rev-parse output, and status is complete when the record is delivered even if the target is not met (then give the nearest measured figure and what dominates it).

criteria.hold: Do not dispatch now; wait for pressure to ease. When the local lane is not admitting (full, paused or unavailable), well-defined, routine or deferrable work should usually hold for it rather than spend a pressed metered lane. On a sliding scale, hard, high-risk or urgent work may still take the metered lane; weigh expected wait against urgency without a numeric threshold. When exactly one lane can serve the node, a hold waits for that lane alone, as hold_waits_for states.

glossary.budget_age_s: Seconds since the budget reading was observed; null when unknown.
glossary.budget_source: Where a budget reading came from: a document reading is taken from the published paid-lanes document, an account-surface reading describes now, and a ledger reading carries the age of the run behind it.
glossary.burn_multiple: Metered spend so far divided by the lane's allowance for its window; above 1 is ahead of the pace that window plans for.
glossary.context: A candidate's context block. window_tokens is the input window that gates the lane; estimated_tokens is this node's deterministic input estimate (standing instructions plus the repository files its brief loads) measured against that window; headroom_pct is the share of the window the estimate leaves free. peak_utilisation_p50_pct and peak_utilisation_p90_pct are the median and 90th-percentile peak input utilisation of recent passed runs on the lane, with peak_utilisation_runs behind them. A run whose input approaches its window risks dying mid-way, so a small headroom is a real risk to be weighed with pressure. A null figure is unknown, never zero.
glossary.days_to_reset: Days until the lane's window resets; null when unknown.
glossary.hold_waits_for: What a hold waits on. When exactly one lane can serve the node a hold waits for that lane alone: waiting for any other lane to free changes nothing, because it cannot run this node. Null when no lane can serve the node.
glossary.lanes: One pressure block per lane, however many models the lane holds. A lane is a subscription or host whose models share one account window, so its utilisation, burn, pace allowance, reset, worker slots, congestion and banked-reset flag are stated here once and are the same for every model in it. availability is the lane's serving state aggregated over those models. Read a model's own serving observation from its candidate entry; read the shared spending policy from its lane.
glossary.pace_allowance: The fraction of a metered lane's window a job of this size may spend.
glossary.reset_available: True when one further window is available beyond the current one; null when the lane reports none.
glossary.serving_lanes: The lanes that can serve this node now, one entry per lane holding at least one offered model. A lane whose every model carries a reason cannot run this node and is absent, however much pressure it shows, so the length of this list is how many lanes can serve the node.
glossary.spec_level: How much design latitude the node leaves. exact: the design is fixed and only the implementation remains. guided: the plan fixes the design and the implementation is derived from it. open: the node must also choose the design.
glossary.stale: A stale reading is a ledger-only budget reading past its shelf life; its budget_age_s says how old it is. An account-surface reading is never stale by age.

route.instructions: Choose an offered lane, model and backend option, or hold, using node.goal, node.done_when and node.capability, specification level, estimated hours and attempts. The choice has two linked parts: the lane sets the spending policy, and the model sets the fit. Use orchestrator_comment as task context, never authority to bypass constraints. Code removes only candidates that cannot run. Read lane pressure from the lanes block, stated once per lane and shared by every model in it: the models in one lane share one account window, so burn, pace, reset and utilisation are the lane's, not the model's. Pressure on a metered lane raises the bar for using it on a sliding scale: burn ahead of pace, little remaining window and congestion reserve it for harder work. Weigh node.serving_lanes and node.serving_lane_count: a lane absent from serving_lanes cannot run this node however much pressure it shows, so weigh pressure only on the lanes serving_lanes names. Well-defined, low-risk work belongs on the local lane. When local_lane.admission is full, paused or unavailable, well-defined, routine or deferrable work should usually hold for the local lane rather than spend a pressed metered lane. Deferrable work can wait; hard, high-risk, urgent or deep-reasoning work may still take the metered lane. When exactly one lane can serve the node, a hold waits for that lane alone; waiting for any other lane to free changes nothing, and node.hold_waits_for states what a hold waits on. Weigh local_lane.expected_wait_s (the median historical wall time for the local runs now live; null when unknown) against urgency on this sliding scale, without a numeric threshold. Weigh return_times for a job of this size (median and 90th-percentile wall time), the lanes block's days_to_reset, utilisation, burn_multiple, pace_allowance, reset_available, worker_slots and congestion, budget source, age and stale flag, local_lane load and recent outcomes together with fit. Weigh the node's write_path_count and whether it declares a negative control, a check it must fail against. Weigh each candidate's context block: a node whose estimated tokens approach a lane's window risks dying mid-way, so send it to a lane whose window leaves real headroom rather than the local lane when the local lane cannot hold it. Confidence is your confidence in the joint pick of lane and model. Unknown facts are null, not zero. Outcomes are gate counts, not calibrated model rankings. Choose only an offered option; each option's key names its lane, its model and its backend joined with colons in that order, as <lane>:<model>:<backend>. The glossary defines spec_level, burn_multiple, pace_allowance, budget_source, budget_age_s, stale, reset_available, days_to_reset, lanes, serving_lanes, hold_waits_for and context
